tech.heading: Currently using
tech.description: Not a complete stack list, but the tools I keep reaching for while connecting research, product work, and personal systems.

python.description: My main language for experiments, data handling, local AI pipelines, and fast idea checks.

colab.description: A lightweight entry point for temporary experiments, model checks, and remote GPU notebooks.

jupyter.description: Keeps data exploration, experiment traces, and reproducible analysis in the same context.

pytorch.description: The deep learning framework I reach for most in multimodal recognition and model prototypes.

numpy.description: The base layer for experimental data, signal features, and model pre/post-processing.

typescript.description: My default for product prototypes, frontend state, and maintainable system boundaries.

react.description: Used for interaction-heavy tools, product surfaces, and experimental interfaces.

rust.description: Useful for local performance, desktop apps, and system parts that need firm boundaries.

next.description: A good fit when content, product experience, and server-side capability meet.

node.description: The everyday runtime for APIs, scripts, data handling, and fast engineering prototypes.

docker.description: Keeps research environments, service dependencies, and deployment paths reproducible.

vue.description: A comfortable UI layer for content systems and lightweight interaction work.

nuxt.description: The framework behind this site, handling content, localization, and page experience.

javascript.description: Still the fastest base for browser experiments, small tools, and quick idea checks.

expo.description: One of the fastest paths into mobile AI workflows and cross-platform prototypes.

tauri.description: A lightweight shell for local-first desktop tools and local AI pipelines.

zotero.description: Core infrastructure for reading, citation management, and long-term research memory.

obsidian.description: A workspace for personal knowledge, project notes, and long-term memory systems.

cplusplus.description: Still important for local AI, audio/video work, and performance-sensitive modules.

turborepo.description: Helps keep multi-app and multi-package prototypes moving together.

tailwind.description: Lets interface work move quickly while keeping tool surfaces consistent.

gitea.description: Self-hostable code and collaboration infrastructure for long-lived personal systems.

vite.description: Keeps frontend experiments and component prototypes close to instant.

electron.description: Still practical when mature desktop capability and a web stack need to meet.

reactNative.description: Connects mobile interaction, capture flows, and personal workflow prototypes.

vscode.description: My main editor for daily engineering, AI-assisted development, and research code.

xcode.description: Used for iOS prototypes, device debugging, and validating mobile interaction details.

postman.description: Useful for API checks, service boundaries, and keeping interface workflows clear.

localFirst.title: Local-first AI tools

interface.title: Dense product interfaces

languages.title: Bridge across languages

work.title: The strongest proof should be software.
work.description: Instead of listing a stack in isolation, I prefer showing how the tools appear inside shipped or active projects.
work.leclog: Leclog is a local-first macOS desktop app for lecture recording, transcription, and session resource management. It combines a React and TypeScript interface with Tauri 2, Rust commands, ffmpeg, and whisper.cpp for local transcription workflows.

languages.title: Communication is part of the product surface.
languages.description: For Japanese AI startups, I want this page to show that I can work across local business context, international technical material, and China-related perspective.

site.title: This is not only a blog. It is my long-term personal system.
site.summary: I use this site to connect writing, concept notes, project records, multilingual content, and software experiments. It is a portfolio, a knowledge base, and a place where unfinished ideas can become usable tools.

writing.title: Writing as a build log
writing.description: Essays and notes preserve the reasoning behind technical choices, failed attempts, and the slow shape of a project.

concepts.title: Concepts as working nodes

projects.title: Projects as evidence

languages.title: Multilingual by default
languages.description: The site keeps Chinese, Japanese, and English close together because my work and job search sit between those contexts.

build.title: A small product, maintained like a product.
build.body1: The site is built with Nuxt, Nuxt Content, i18n, and a content model that lets projects, concepts, notes, and essays reference one another.
build.body2: That matters because the site itself demonstrates how I think about tools: keep the system understandable, make the content durable, and let small pieces accumulate into a useful interface.
